scenes.text: Why do newly independent states struggle to enforce laws despite powerful governments?
scenes.narration: Imagine gaining freedom after centuries of colonial rule, yet discovering your new government cannot deliver development. Why did post-colonial nations find it so difficult to govern effectively?

scenes.text: A heavy imported tractor engine bolted onto an old wooden farming cart.
scenes.narration: Think of this analogy: colonial rulers left behind an enormous, modern administrative engine, but the society underneath remained deeply traditional. The vehicle simply cannot run smoothly.

scenes.name: Gunnar Myrdal
scenes.idea: India is a soft state with limited capacity to enforce laws.
scenes.narration: Gunnar Myrdal coined the term soft state for India in his study Asian Drama. A soft state passes grand laws but shows very poor implementation on the ground.

scenes.heading: Why Are States Soft?
items: Disobedience culture inherited from the freedom struggle
Cultural tendency where lawbreakers gain social respect
Galbraith called this condition a functional anarchy
scenes.narration: Here is the trick to remember Myrdal's point: corruption, Gandhi's tradition of civil disobedience, and social habits created weak law enforcement. Political scientist Galbraith even labeled India a functional anarchy.

scenes.heading: Dependency School Pyramid
scenes.narration: Marxist dependency theorists like Frank and Wallerstein argued that global capitalism creates unequal exchange. Wealth flows upward to core nations, leaving peripheral satellites trapped in underdevelopment.

scenes.name: Hamza Alavi
scenes.idea: Post-colonial states are overdeveloped institutions inherited from colonial rule.
scenes.narration: Pakistani scholar Hamza Alavi introduced the theory of the overdeveloped state. He explained that colonial rulers built an oversized state machinery that continues to dominate post-colonial societies.

scenes.heading: Western versus Post-Colonial States

columns.title: Western State
items: Perfect match of economy and politics

scenes.narration: Notice the major difference: Western states grew naturally alongside their business class, while post-colonial states inherited foreign structures where military and civil officials mediate between competing classes.

items: Myrdal identified soft states with poor policy implementation
Dependency school exposed core-periphery exploitation and underdevelopment
Alavi explained overdeveloped states ruled by bureaucratic oligarchies
scenes.narration: Here is your quick recap. Remember how Myrdal diagnosed soft states, dependency theorists revealed global core-periphery inequality, and Alavi showed how colonial legacies created overdeveloped, executive-heavy states.
